title: A globally generated invertible sheaf has finitely many sections covering a quasi-compact scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $\mathcal L$ be a globally generated invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Then there are finitely many global sections $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ of $\mathcal L$ such that $X=\bigcup_{j=1}^m X_{t_j}$, where $X_{t_j}$ is the nonvanishing locus defined in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NC (varieties-lemma-enough-globally-generated-ample), proof, sentence beginning 'Again because X is quasi-compact'

proof.text: Apply globalGeneration_nonvanishing_cover [lem-sc-global-generation-nonvanishing-cover] to obtain that all global sections have nonvanishing loci covering X.

For each section s, rewrite its nonvanishing locus using nonvanishingLocus_eq_compl_support_zeroLocus [lem-weil-pbc-section-nonvanishing-zero-locus]. The complement of the support of Hom.zeroLocus (homOfGlobalSection L s) is an open subset, so the rewritten set is open. This gives the openness needed by the compactness step without assuming ampleness.

Apply Mathlib IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover to isCompact_univ, the nonvanishing loci, their openness, and the covering equality. Quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] gives a Finset S of global sections covering X. Enumerate S using S.equivFin and define t(j) as the underlying section of the inverse image of j. For each point x, extract s in S whose locus contains x; its index under the equivalence supplies membership in the union of the loci of t. Hence this union equals Set.univ. The argument also works for the empty scheme and an empty finite subcover.
